summary: Amazonas department stands under Colombia's national framework. The source inventory contains no finding specific to the department: no departmental or municipal law, enforcement practice, recorded incident or local institution in Amazonas is documented in it, so the national assessment for Colombia applies without regional qualification.
tangentialFactors: No comparison between Amazonas and other Colombian departments is available in the inventory. The region-level material it does hold describes a sub-national unit of the same name in a different country and has no bearing on Colombia.
localsOnly: No resident-facing finding specific to Amazonas department is sourced. Rules on identity documents, health care, facilities and partner recognition for people living in Amazonas are set by Colombian national law and are carried by Colombia's national assessment.
outOfScopeNotes:
The inventory's region-level sources describe Amazonas state in Brazil, not the Colombian department. They set out Brazilian state and municipal rules with no legal force in Colombia: a Manaus municipal ban on multigender restrooms signed on 18 October 2022; Amazonas State Law No. 7,552 of 10 June 2025 barring gender-affirming care for minors under 18; State Law No. 6,463 of 10 October 2023 prohibiting neutral language and non-binary forms of address in school curricula, teaching materials and official documents; and State Law 6,469/2023 restricting children's participation in pride parades. They further describe Brazilian registry practice for gender-marker changes and a 2022 case in Manaus in which recognition of a non-binary identity required six months of insistence and intervention by a public defender's office. None of this can be attributed to Amazonas department, Colombia, and none of it is carried into the assessment above.

Two sources in the inventory report national Colombian figures and state explicitly that they contain no information on Amazonas; those figures belong to Colombia's national assessment, not to this record.

Whether Amazonas department has its own ordinances, departmental health or security protocols, or recorded anti-trans incidents is unresolved: no source in the inventory addresses the question.
